newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Former Austria finmin to tackle EU unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Former Austria finmin to tackle EU unemployment.

text.p: Former Austrian Finance Minister Ferdinand Lacina will become Chancellor Viktor Klima's special envoy to the European Union on employment issues, Klima's office said on Wednesday.

A spokesman for Klima said Lacina's appointment followed a decision by Europe's Social Democrats to nominate a personal representative for each party leader. They will work together to draw up recommendations to safeguard EU jobs.
"We must fight the intolerably high levels of unemployment at a national and at an EU level," Lacina, 54, told the Austrian news agency APA in a first reaction to his new job.
"We have to look seriously at how the United States has managed to increase employment. I am willing to learn."
Lacina drew a line under 13 years in politics in March 1995 when he resigned as finance minister, a post he had occupied for eight years.
Last year he took over as chief executive of bank GiroCredit. His term will end in September when GiroCredit's takeover by First Austrian savings bank is finalised.
